From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Crestward RFP: PHI controls deep-dive and evidence timeline

Hi Elena —

Thanks for sending the RFP sections focused on PHI handling. I've compiled our technical responses and a mapping to the Crestward control questions (attached). High level answers below; see attached redwood_phi_response.xlsx and Appendix A for full snippets you can paste into the RFP.

Summary (short):
- Data classification: Redwood treats any customer-provided PII/PHI as sensitive by default. Customers can opt-in fields to be redacted at ingestion.
- Data residency: Hosted API routes can be pinned to region (US/EU) per customer; Dedicated/Private deployments can be run entirely inside customer VPCs.
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256-GCM at rest for model weights, caches, and stored artifacts. KMS-managed keys with automated rotation.
- PHI in logs: We do not persist request bodies in plaintext for customers that opt into our PHI retention setting. Primary logs are metadata-only; access to token-level traces requires approvals and is gated to SOC2 roles.
- Access control and auditing: RBAC via SSO (SAML/OIDC) + granular workspace roles. Audit logs retained per contract (default 90 days, configurable).
- KV cache and prompt handling: Prefix/KV caching is customer-configurable; when customers enable PHI-safe mode we disable cross-customer caching and enforce stricter TTLs.
- De-identification: We provide guidance and tooling examples (see Appendix A) for deterministic redaction and a recommended post-processing step to remove names/SSNs before long-term storage.
- Incident response: We have documented IR runbooks and SLA-backed notification timelines for confirmed data exposures.

Requested evidence and timeline:
- SOC 2 Type II summary: available (redacted) — 2 business days to provide PDF.
- Sample audit log entries (anonymized): 3 business days.
- KMS key rotation policy and a rotation event log: 4 business days.
- Network/dataflow diagrams with ingress/egress callouts: 2 business days.

Attachments: Crestward_RFP_Appendix_A.pdf (text snippets), redwood_phi_response.xlsx (control mapping).

If you want, we can schedule a 45-minute technical call next week to walk through the evidence and any redlines.

Best,

Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.ai

Dylan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few clarifications before we loop procurement/legal:

1) For "PHI-safe mode" can you confirm whether request bodies are excluded from all long-term logs (not just traces)? We need an assurance that request bodies containing PHI are not retained longer than processing unless Customer explicitly opts in.
2) For KMS key rotation: do you support external (customer-managed) keys in Dedicated/Private, and what is the process for rotating an external key?
3) On audit logs: we need a sample showing username, timestamp, action, resource, and outcome for a read of model output containing PHI. Anonymized is fine; make sure the schema matches the table we shared in the RFP (Q4.b).

Also our security team would like to see a redacted SOC 2 report and a timeline for when the full evidence bundle would be ready. Could you include the runbook reference for breach notification timing so our legal team can review?

If possible, could you share the SOC 2 summary and a 1–page executive summary for procurement by end of next week?

Thanks,
Elena
Senior Security Program Manager, Crestward Health
security@crestward.com
